Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 45, verses 1–2:

(p-5317) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Jathiyah

It is named so because its verses contain an explanation of the cause for the delay of the Resurrection until the Day of Judgment, namely the gathering of the nations for judgment before Allah the Exalted and His separating them on the Day of Judgment. It is among the noble themes of the Qur'an. It is also called "Surat al-Shari'ah" (the Surah of the Sacred Law), because its verses contain the manner in which this Sharia abrogates (naskh) all other laws and its superiority over them. This is also among the valuable themes in it. So said al-Mahayimi.

It is a Meccan surah. Some scholars excepted from it the verse: ﴿Say to those who believe: Forgive those who do not hope for the days of Allah﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 14], for it has been said that it is Medinan, revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), as will come. Its number of verses is thirty-seven.

(p-5318) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion of the interpretation of His, the Exalted, saying:

[1, 2] ﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 2].

﴿Ha Mim﴾ ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 2]. Al-Mahayimi said: His might requires the bestowing of proofs by which victory over adversaries is achieved, and the bestowing of perfections that are difficult to attain, and the kinds of felicities, the sharpness of insight. And His wisdom requires the erasing of doubts, the removal of deficiencies, the burning away of wretchedness, and the preparing of thought. He sent it down from the station of His might in accordance with the requirement of His wisdom, to perfect the theoretical and practical faculties, so that through them one may reach the true perfections: faith, certainty, and intellect. This is in view of the kinds of signs that contain proofs and the removal of doubts. Among them are the signs of bodies (ayat al-ajsam).

The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:

[13] ﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.﴾

﴿And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all of it from Him. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.﴾ That is: in the signs of Allah, His proofs and His evidences, through which they take heed and give thought. Al-Mahayimi (al-Mahayimi) said: Among them is that the linking of part of the world to part is evidence of His oneness; that making some of it the cause of other parts is evidence of His wisdom; and that making the whole subjected to man is evidence of the perfection of His generosity. So whoever denies these signs and does not give thanks for these blessings deserves the gravest forms of retribution.

(p-5321) The discussion of the interpretation of His words, Exalted is He:

[14] ﴿Say to those who believe: let them forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah, so that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn.﴾

﴿Say to those who believe﴾, i.e., who have affirmed belief in Allah and followed you. ﴿Let them forgive those who do not expect the Days of Allah﴾, i.e., who do not fear the severity of Allah, His vengeance, and His encounters with His enemies. ﴿So that He may recompense a people for what they used to earn﴾, i.e., for their knowledge. From it comes pardoning and overlooking some of what harms and alienates. It has been narrated that it was revealed concerning ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu), when a man of Ghifar had insulted him, and he intended to seize him, so the verse would be Madani. It was said: what supports this is the objection raised against its being Meccan, that those who believed in it were oppressed, so they could not retaliate against them, and one who is powerless is not commanded to pardon and overlook. It was answered that the intended meaning is that he does this between himself and Allah in his heart, so that he may be rewarded for it, along with the fact that the continuous powerlessness of each one of them is not known. Therefore the correct view is that the verse is Meccan, like the surah. And the meaning of its being revealed concerning ʿUmar, if it is sound, is that it applies to his case, and that it is cited as evidence for his forbearance, as we have verified the intended meaning of revelation (nuzul) more than once.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 45, verse 15:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self; and whoever does evil, it is against it. Then to your Lord you will be returned.﴾

﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self﴾: i.e., because he has freed it (nafs) from the punishment. ﴿And whoever does evil, it is against it﴾: i.e., he has done wrong in his deed by disobeying his Lord, so he has committed an offence against himself, for he has ruined it thereby. ﴿Then to your Lord you will be returned﴾: i.e., you will go back (to Him). So He will recompense the good-doer for his goodness, and the evil-doer for his evil.

The Commentary on the Words of Allah, the Exalted:

[16] ﴿And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture and authority and prophethood, and provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds.﴾

(p-5322) ﴿And We had certainly given the Children of Israel the Scripture﴾: that is, the Torah. ﴿And authority﴾: that is, understanding of the Scripture and knowledge of the sunan (prophetic ways and precedents) that descend with the Scripture. ﴿And prophethood﴾: that is, We made among them prophets and messengers to the creation. ﴿And provided them with good things﴾: meaning the manna and the quails. ﴿And preferred them over the worlds﴾: that is, over the worlds of the people of their time, by giving them what He did not give others, as Allah, the Exalted, said:

On the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

[17] ﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter. And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ.﴾

﴿And We gave them clear proofs concerning the matter﴾ meaning: proofs, demonstrations, and decisive evidences that repel disagreement. But they refused except to disagree. ﴿And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of rivalry among themselves﴾ meaning: out of their own injustice and transgression, seeking immediate worldly interests. ﴿Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which they used to differ﴾ meaning: by way of reckoning and recompense. [22] ﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth, and that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.﴾

﴿And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth﴾ i.e., with wisdom and rightness. **Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 45, verses 23–24:**

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[23, 24] ﴿Have you seen one who has taken his own desire as his god, and Allah has misguided him knowingly, and has sealed his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a veil? Who then will guide him after Allah? Will you not then take heed?﴾ ﴿And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time." And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture.﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24].

﴿Have you seen one who has taken his own desire as his god﴾: that is, one who has abandoned following guidance in favour of following desire, so that he worships it, and thus has made it a god. It is an eloquent simile (tashbih baligh) or a metaphor (isti'arah). Al-Qashani said: "The ilah (god) is the one worshipped. When they obeyed desire, they had worshipped it and made it a god, since whatever a person worships through his love and obedience is his god, even if it were a stone!" ﴿And Allah has misguided him knowingly﴾: that is, while knowing his condition, through the loss of his readiness (for guidance) and the turning of his face toward the lower direction. Or, (the phrase may mean) that this worshipper of desire, while knowing what he is obliged to do in religion, is, under the reading that ﴿knowingly﴾ (ʿalā ʿilm) is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the pronoun object in "Allah has misguided him" and not to the subject, then the failure (ikhlāl) is due to his acting contrary to his knowledge, and his foot slips away from his insight, because his heart is saturated with love of the self and the dominance of desire. Or (it means) "knowingly" in a sense of knowledge that is not beneficial, because it belongs to the category of superfluities, containing no path or arrival toward the Truth. ﴿And has sealed his hearing and his heart﴾: that is, by expulsion from the gate of guidance and distancing from the place where the words of the Truth are heard and understood, because of the presence of rust (rayn) and the thickness of the veil, so that he comprehends nothing from it. ﴿And placed over his sight a veil﴾: that is, preventing him from seeing the proofs and signs of Allah. ﴿Who then will guide him after Allah﴾: that is, who will grant him success in reaching the Truth after Allah has misguided him? ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾

﴿And they say, "There is not but our worldly life"﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24]: that is, there is no life, or no state, other than this life of ours in which we are: ﴿we die﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24], that is, by natural bodily death; ﴿and we live﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24], that is, the physical, sensory life. There is neither death nor life other than these two. ﴿And nothing destroys us except time﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24], that is, the passing of nights and days and the length of life. ﴿And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24]: that is, they do not say this on the basis of knowledge, but on the basis of supposition and guesswork. The word "that" (dhālika) refers either to the attribution of events to time, or to the denial of resurrection, or to both.

Al-Zamakhshari said: They used to claim that the passing of days and nights is what affects the destruction of souls, and they denied the Angel of Death and his taking of souls by the command of Allah. They used to attribute every occurrence and event to the dahr (time) and the zaman (age). Their poetry is full of complaints about time. From this is His saying ﷺ: "Do not revile time, for Allah is time" (ﷺ), that is, Allah is the One who brings the events, not time. End.

Al-Khattabi said: Its meaning is: I am the Lord of time and the Manager of the affairs that you attribute to time. Whoever reviles time because it is the doer of these affairs, his reviling returns to his Lord, who is their doer. Time is merely a period placed as a container for the occurrence of affairs. It was their custom, when some hardship befell them, to attribute it to time, saying, "Woe to time!" and "Ruin to time!" End.

Ibn Kathir said: Ibn Hazm erred, and whoever follows his path among the Zahiriyyah (the literalist school), in counting "al-Dahr" among the Most Beautiful Names, taking it from this hadith. End.

A note:

In this verse there is a refutation of the Dahriyyah (the materialists who deny a Creator), who are the Mu'attilah, in that their basis is conjecture and guesswork. They have not smelled the fragrance of certainty. Whatever is of this nature, the gate of acceptance is closed against it: ﴿Indeed, conjecture avails nothing against the truth﴾ [Yunus: 36].

Al-Shahrastani said regarding the Mu'attilah of the Arabs: "A category of them denied the Creator, the resurrection, and the restoration, and they spoke of nature (al-tab') as the giver of life and time as the destroyer. They are the ones about whom the Glorious Qur'an informed: ﴿And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we die and we live"﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24], pointing to the sensible natures in the lower world, and to the restriction of life and death to their composition and dissolution."

So the unifying principle is nature (al-tab'), and the destroyer is time: ﴿And nothing destroys us except time. And they have no knowledge of that; they only conjecture﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 24]. Thus they were refuted by necessary intellectual proofs and innate signs, in many a verse and surah. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have they not reflected? There is no madness in their companion; he is but a clear warner﴾ [al-A'raf: 184]. ﴿Have they not looked into the dominion of the heavens and the earth?﴾ [al-A'raf: 185]. He said: ﴿Have they not looked at what Allah has created?﴾ [al-Nahl: 48]. He said: ﴿Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days?"﴾ [Fussilat: 9]. He said: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21]. Thus the necessary proof from creation to the Creator was established, for He is capable of perfection in both beginning and restoration. End.

For me, in the refutation of the Dahriyyah, who are the materialists and naturalists, there is a book whose title is "Dala'il al-Tawhid" (Proofs of Divine Unity). Let the seeker refer to it, for beyond it there is, by the praise of Allah, the Exalted, no further addition.

(p-5329) The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[32] ﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour—there is no doubt concerning it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is. We only assume it to be a supposition, and we are not certain."﴾

﴿And when it was said, "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true, and the Hour—there is no doubt concerning it," you said, "We do not know what the Hour is"﴾ meaning: What is it? That is, we are not certain of it. ﴿We only assume it to be a supposition, and we are not certain﴾ meaning: that it is coming and will certainly occur.

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[33–35] ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they did, and there will befall them what they used to mock.﴾ ﴿And it will be said, "Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day, and your abode is the Fire, and you have no helpers."﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34] ﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the life of this world deceived you." So today they will not be brought out of it, nor will they be allowed to make amends.﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35]

﴿And there appeared to them the evils of what they did﴾, i.e., the ugly things of their deeds, or the punishments of their evil deeds. ﴿And there befell them what they used to mock﴾, meaning the recompense.

﴿Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this your Day﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34], i.e., We will leave you in the punishment as one leaves what is forgotten, just as you neglected preparation for it. As for ﴿We forget you﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34], it is a metaphor (istiʿarah) or a sent metonymy (majaz mursal).

﴿And your abode is the Fire, and you have no helpers﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 34]. ﴿That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery, and the life of this world deceived you﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35], i.e., it deluded you until you preferred it over the Hereafter and assumed that there is no life other than it. ﴿So today they will not be brought out of it﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35], i.e., out of the Fire. ﴿Nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 35], i.e., it will not be asked of them that they appease their Lord, that is, satisfy Him, from al-iʿtab (removing reproach). This is an allusion (kinayah) to gaining His satisfaction. Alternatively, it means: they will not be returned to the world so that they may repent and turn back in penitence, for after death there is no opportunity to make amends.

(p-٥٣٣٠)The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[36, 37] ﴿So to Allah belongs all praise, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds. And to Him belongs grandeur throughout the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 36-37].

﴿So to Allah belongs all praise﴾: that is, complete commendation. Ibn Jarir said: That is, to Allah belongs all praise for His blessings and His favours upon His creation. So praise Him alone, O people, for all the blessing you have comes from Him, not from what you worship besides Him of gods and idols. ﴿Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 36]. ﴿And to Him belongs grandeur throughout the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 37]: that is, supremacy, the utmost of exaltation and greatness over everything, and the ultimate of loftiness and majesty through His being free of need from them and their being in need of Him. ﴿And He is the Almighty﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 37]: that is, the Strong, the Subduer of everything. ﴿The All-Wise﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 37]. Al-Qashani said: That is, the One who arranges the readiness of every thing, by the subtlety of His management, preparing it to accept what He wills from it of His attributes, through the precision of His craftsmanship and the hidden depth of His wisdom (there is no god but Him, the Lord of the worlds).
